summary: Redwood hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for OceanSearch's use case: improving e-commerce search relevance across product catalogs. Discussed architecture (embeddings, vector store, rerank step), tradeoffs (latency vs cost, recall vs precision), security questions (SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency), and next steps for a 1-week POC. Customer is interested in hosted API to move quickly but flagged potential need for VPC later.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-30 10:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Marcus (Redwood); Maya, Liam, Rachel, Noah (OceanSearch)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE, with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Marcus from product — we'll walk through embeddings + rerank today, run through console quickstart, and then talk POC next steps.
00:23 Maya Thompson: Thanks — appreciate it. Quick note we have about 40 minutes, i pulled in Liam and Rachel cause they'll be owners of the POC and security review.
00:35 Priya Nair: Great. I'll start with high-level flow, then demo the hosted API endpoints (embeddings -> vector search -> rerank), and show some Console screenshots for monitoring and Optimize tips.
00:50 Priya Nair: So the typical flow we recommend is: you call the embeddings endpoint to get vectors for your docs, store them in your vector DB of choice or Redwood vectors, then at query time we do a k-NN to get candidates and optionally call the rerank endpoint to rescore the top K using the full context. The rerank model uses a cross-encoder style reranker which improves precision on top results.
01:20 Liam Ortiz: Quick question — is Redwood returning the vectors for us to store, or do you host a vector store? We currently use Elastic clusters with approximate nearest neighbor.
01:33 Priya Nair: You can do either. Hosted API returns the embeddings and you store them in Elastic or Pinecone; we also have a managed vectors option inside Redwood but for POC most customers bring their own vector store. We show examples for Elastic & Redis in the docs.
01:50 Noah Patel: What's the expected latency if we do embeddings + rerank on say top 20? Our SLO is 200ms P50 during peak.
02:03 Marcus Yu: Good Q. For hosted, typical embeddings call is 10-30ms per vector depending on model and size; k-NN lookup is external. The rerank step adds cost/latency — expect 40-120ms for reranking top 10-20 on a hosted cross-encoder if you use our small rerank model. So one roundtrip can be around 120-200ms end-to-end if you optimize. There's tradeoff but we can show batching/caching via Console Optimize to reduce cost/latency.
02:38 Rachel Kim: And security — we need SOC2 + SSO and encryption at rest. Also would like KMS integration for keys, and audit logs.
02:51 Jordan Lee: Yep we have SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/Okta, KMS integrations and detailed audit logs. i'll attach the security pack after the call.
03:05 Maya Thompson: Curious about data residency — some EU data may need to stay in EU region.
03:12 Priya Nair: For hosted we have region routing; you can pin requests to eu-west region. For stricter regs we also offer Private (VPC) deployments. For the POC you can try hosted with eu region.
03:28 Priya Nair: i'll demo a quick embedding call now — bear with me while i share screen.
03:40 [screen share noise; brief pause]
03:50 Priya Nair: Here's a sample curl for embeddings: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":"nike air max"}' — response is a dense vector. Note transcription sometimes shows rwd-emb--, sorry that was me typing.
04:20 Noah Patel: Any concerns with vector dimensionality mismatch if we re-index?
04:28 Priya Nair: We standardize dimensionality per model; if you re-index with a new model you'll want to re-embed docs or use cross-model similarity heuristics, which we've covered in the docs.
04:45 Marcus Yu: Also Optimize can recommend quantized model variants for cost savings on embeddings heavy workloads.
05:00 Liam Ortiz: Walk us through the rerank request and what you send back to the client.
05:08 Priya Nair: Rerank endpoint example: POST /v1/rerank with candidate list plus query + doc context. We return scores and an ordering. Important to pass the original doc text or condensed context; reranker uses full cross-attention so sending the best context helps.
05:35 Jordan Lee: For ecomm, customers typically do a first-pass semantic recall with embeddings (high recall) and then rerank to boost relevance and brand filters.
05:50 Maya Thompson: Wondering about negative signals — user clicks, returns — can rerank incorporate such signals?
05:58 Priya Nair: Rerank is model-driven but you can apply business rules post-score. Another pattern is to fine-tune a custom rerank model or apply a small linear model combining model scores + signals. For quick wins we suggest a hybrid: rerank scores + business filters.
06:25 Rachel Kim: How long does it take to sign an enterprise contract? We have procurement timelines.
06:33 Jordan Lee: Typical is 4-8 weeks for standard contracts; for POC we can do a short EULA and usage agreement to get started faster.
06:45 Priya Nair: i'm going to show the Console: here's per-route latency, token cost breakdown, and a rerank dashboard which shows before/after results and regression alerts tied to eval prompts.
07:05 [screen scrolls]
07:20 Priya Nair: You can also enable token-level billing attribution to see how much rerank adds in dollars per query. For example, a 10-doc rerank might add 2-3x token cost compared to embeddings + recall alone depending on model.
07:45 Liam Ortiz: Can we set an automatic fallback to a cheaper rerank if latency spikes?
07:52 Priya Nair: Yes — routing policies can fallback to a smaller rerank or skip rerank and return semantic-only results. We show canary rollouts and A/B within Console.
08:10 Maya Thompson: Could you share typical POC metrics we should measure?
08:18 Marcus Yu: Sure — we recommend: precision@k, click-through lift, mean reciprocal rank, latency P50/P95, and cost per query. We'll include a POC template.
08:35 Noah Patel: Any guidance on vector store structure for catalog — one doc per SKU or aggregated pages?
08:43 Priya Nair: For ecomm we usually index per SKU with additional context like product description + specs + title + synonyms. Some customers add category-level embeddings for hierarchical recall.
09:05 Rachel Kim: On encryption — if we send data to hosted, is that encrypted at rest under our KMS?
09:12 Jordan Lee: Yes, data at rest in our managed vectors can be encrypted with customer-managed keys; we'll share the KMS integration guide.
09:25 Maya Thompson: If we move to Dedicated or Private later, what does the migration look like?
09:32 Priya Nair: We have migration docs — typically you repoint endpoints to Dedicated and re-sync vector data; for Private we can run an on-prem package. We'll help with step-by-step and it's a one-time migration.
09:50 [brief cross talk: someone background noise]
10:05 Priya Nair: i'm going to demo a live query: 1) embed query, 2) retrieve top 50 from Elastic, 3) rerank top 10. I'll run the example — results should show ordering improvements and rerank scores.
10:25 [demo running]
11:10 Priya Nair: Ok example result before rerank: product A, product B, product C; after rerank we boosted product B because title and specs matched query intent. You can see scores returned from /v1/rerank: score values 0.78, 0.65 etc.
11:40 Liam Ortiz: The score scale — is it calibrated across models?
11:45 Priya Nair: Scores are relative per model, we recommend normalizing or using rank-only for production. Console's evals can compare models and suggest thresholds.
12:05 Maya Thompson: Let's talk cost: we're running millions of queries monthly. How do customers optimize?
12:15 Marcus Yu: Batching, prefix caching, and quantized embedding models. Also do a hybrid approach: semantic recall at cheap small model, rerank only top N, or do a learned cascade. Optimize suggests policies based on your trace data.
12:40 Rachel Kim: For legal, we need data processing agreement and subprocessors list.
12:47 Jordan Lee: We'll attach DPA and our subprocessors, and happy to run through.
13:00 Maya Thompson: Any red flags we should look out for during POC?
13:05 Priya Nair: Watch label drift — if you change embeddings model mid-POC you'll need to re-embed. Also track distribution shift so rerank stays calibrated. We'll help instrument evals.
13:25 Noah Patel: Can we test with our sample catalog of 150k SKUs in POC?
13:31 Jordan Lee: Yes that's within scope for hosted. We'll size together and may recommend a reserved burst or sample subset depending on load.
13:45 Priya Nair: for the sample POC, we suggest 1) ingest 10k representative docs, 2) run eval prompt set and run baseline metrics, 3) iterate rerank thresholds.
14:05 Liam Ortiz: Any sandbox keys can we use?
14:10 Jordan Lee: We'll provide sandbox creds and a short-term key for the POC — i'll include instructions.
14:20 [screen note: link pasted in chat]
14:28 Priya Nair: Now quick note on model variants: we have small rerank models for low latency and larger ones for accuracy. Console Optimize will recommend which model based on your evals.
14:45 Maya Thompson: Does the rerank use user logs for training? Privacy concerns.
14:52 Priya Nair: We don't use production data to train models without explicit opt-in. You can also opt-out of data collection for hosted.
15:05 Jordan Lee: ok let's capture next steps — Jordan to send pricing and security pack; Priya to share rerank sample code + bench spreadsheet; Maya to confirm POC stakeholders and success criteria.
15:20 Maya Thompson: Sounds good — tentatively let's schedule POC kickoff week of 10/11.
15:30 Rachel Kim: we'll aim to review security pack same week.
15:40 [closing pleasantries]
15:50 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
16:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts like rwd-embed vs rwd-embed-1 and minor speaker mislabels. References to shared deck and spreadsheet in chat.
